title: A split-GAL4 driver line resource for Drosophila neuron types
abstract: Techniques that enable precise manipulations of subsets of neurons in the fly central nervous system (CNS) have greatly facilitated our understanding of the neural basis of behavior. Split-GAL4 driver lines allow specific targeting of cell types in Drosophila melanogaster and other species. We describe here a collection of 3060 lines targeting a range of cell types in the adult Drosophila CNS and 1373 lines characterized in third-instar larvae. These tools enable functional, transcriptomic, and proteomic studies based on precise anatomical targeting. NeuronBridge and other search tools relate light microscopy images of these split-GAL4 lines to connectomes reconstructed from electron microscopy images. The collections are the result of screening over 77,000 split hemidriver combinations. Previously published and new lines are included, all validated for driver expression and curated for optimal cell-type specificity across diverse cell types. In addition to images and fly stocks for these well-characterized lines, we make available 300,000 new 3D images of other split-GAL4 lines.

elife_assessment.summary: This valuable study presents a resource for researchers using Drosophila to study neural circuits, in the form of a collection of split-Gal4 lines with an online search engine, which will facilitate the mapping of neuronal circuits. The evidence is convincing to demonstrate the utility of these new tools, and of the search engine, for understanding expression patterns in adults and larvae, and differences between the sexes. These resources will be of broad interest to Drosophila researchers in the field of neurobiology.

narrative:
Short impact summary

This eLife resource paper has clear early uptake for a methods-heavy Drosophila neuroscience toolset: it is in the top 10% of its field and year, has 16 OpenAlex citations, and shows 17 documented downstream reuse instances. The journal’s assessment calls it “valuable” with “convincing” evidence, and the citation pattern is especially notable for rapid adoption through preprints and papers in high-visibility venues.

Full narrative

A split-GAL4 driver line resource for Drosophila neuron types is best understood as enabling infrastructure for circuit neuroscience rather than as a single hypothesis-driven study. The paper introduces a large collection of split-GAL4 lines for adult and larval Drosophila central nervous system cell types, along with an online search engine that helps researchers identify useful expression patterns. That combination of biological resource and searchable access appears to be the core of its impact: the work is already being reused downstream and cited by studies focused on Drosophila neurobiology, connectomics, optogenetics, sleep, and circuit dissection.

The citation record suggests unusually fast community take-up for a resource article. Most of the citing works are preprints, and the citing venues include bioRxiv as well as eLife, Nature, Cell, Current Biology, and other established journals. That pattern is consistent with the paper serving as a methodological anchor: researchers appear to be incorporating the driver lines and associated search tools early in project development, before or alongside formal publication.

The downstream reuse signals reinforce that reading. The record shows 17 documented reuse instances, including one dataset citation, and the article is associated with 24 RRID entries, indicating structured reuse of the resource in the literature. Funding from NIH and Howard Hughes Medical Institute also fits a platform-building effort aimed at broad community use rather than a narrow application. Together, these signals point to a well-curated tool paper that is already shaping how other groups target and manipulate Drosophila neurons.

At the same time, the broader attention record is comparatively quiet: there are no captured event-data mentions in the available sources, so the strongest evidence comes from scholarly reuse and citation behavior rather than public discussion. That does not weaken the main story. For a resource paper, the clearest marker of significance is whether other researchers adopt it, and here the evidence shows both breadth and speed of uptake. The eLife assessment is aligned with that picture, describing the study as valuable and the evidence as convincing.
